questions.question: A simple sentence contains what?
choices: two independent clauses joined by a conjunction

questions.question: A compound sentence joins what?
choices: a subject and a verb only

questions.question: A complex sentence contains an independent clause and what?
choices: two complete sentences without a connector

questions.question: Which is a complete independent clause?
Which word often joins independent clauses in a compound sentence?
“Although the rain stopped, the field remained wet.” What kind of sentence is this?
“The bell rang, and students entered.” What structure is used?
“The bell rang.” What structure is used?
“Because the team practiced, its timing improved.” Which part is dependent?
A sentence has two complete clauses joined only by a comma. What error is this?
A writer joins two independent clauses with no punctuation or conjunction. What error is this?
“After the meeting ended.” Why is this usually a fragment in standard edited English?
choices: it is a dependent clause without an independent clause

questions.question: Which revision correctly joins the clauses? “The trail was muddy. We wore boots.”
choices: The trail was muddy, we wore boots.
The trail was muddy because. We wore boots.
Muddy the trail, we wore boots.
The trail was muddy, so we wore boots.

questions.question: Which sentence uses coordination to show two equally important actions?
choices: When I checked the map, Lina packed the water.
I checked the map, and Lina packed the water.
Checking the map. Lina packed the water.
I checked the map Lina packed water.

questions.question: Which is a complex sentence?
choices: We left, and the rain began.
We left when the rain began.

questions.question: Which revision fixes the comma splice? “The road was closed, we took another route.”
choices: The road was closed, so we took another route.
The road was closed, we took another route.
The road was closed because. We took another route.

questions.question: A sentence begins with “After finishing the lab,” but never states who finished it. What should the writer add?
choices: an independent clause that completes the thought

questions.question: A writer uses three dependent clauses but no independent clause. What is the result?
Which choice best combines these ideas without changing their relationship? “The museum opened late. Visitors waited outside.”
choices: Because the museum opened late, visitors waited outside.
The museum opened late, visitors waited outside.
Visitors waited outside the museum opened late.

questions.question: An editor finds a sentence that is grammatically complete but difficult to follow because several ideas are packed into it. What is the best revision strategy?
choices: divide or reorder the ideas while preserving their logical relationships
